Funding
Orakl Oncology Raises $34M Series A to Expand AI Cancer Drug Prediction
Published
November 12, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Norrsken VC announced on November 12, 2026 that it co-led Orakl Oncology’s oversubscribed $34 million Series A alongside Singular, bringing the AI drug-development company’s total funding to $50 million.
Orakl plans to expand its dataset and AI research team, increase data generation fivefold and move beyond colorectal and pancreatic cancers into lung and gastric cancers. The proceeds are also intended to establish US and UK teams, deploy predictions across more than 10 drug programs and discover and validate drug co-targets from patient biology and experimental screens.
New investors InfraVia, Serena, the Patient Autonome Fund managed by Bpifrance, teampact.ventures and Plug and Play joined the round, alongside existing backers Verve Ventures, Speedinvest and HCVC.
Patient-Derived Data and AI
Founded in 2023 as a spin-out of Gustave Roussy, Orakl grows patient-derived tumor organoids, which are laboratory models of individual patients’ cancers, and screens them against drugs. Its platform overview describes results enriched with genomic, transcriptomic and phenotypic data and anchored to longitudinal clinical histories, creating a multimodal dataset for its predictive systems.
Orakl’s biopharma products are divided between O-Predict and O-Target. O-Predict is designed to anticipate trial endpoints including tumor response, progression-free survival and overall survival, identify biomarkers that distinguish likely responders, assess drug combinations and compare benefit-risk profiles. O-Target focuses on therapeutic-target discovery.
Norrsken calls the resulting patient cohorts virtual cancer patients . The drug-response measurements must be generated through patient samples, laboratory infrastructure and hospital partnerships rather than assembled from existing databases. Every experiment adds proprietary data connecting patient biology, clinical information and observed drug responses.
What the SCOPE Preprint Shows
Orakl reports 90% accuracy for prospective predictions of individual patient responses across more than 30 clinical trials. A separate April 2026 preprint co-authored by Orakl staff provides detailed arm-level results for SCOPE, the Screening-to-Clinical Outcome Prediction Engine. It is marked as early-stage research that may not yet have been peer reviewed.
SCOPE was trained on 54 treatment lines from 52 patients with metastatic colorectal or pancreatic cancer, using matched clinical data and organoid screens covering nine compounds. To predict trial outcomes, it generated synthetic patient profiles from published eligibility criteria and matched them to a biobank of 81 patient-derived organoid lines.
External validation covered 32 arms from 23 published trials. The authors report an R² of 0.85 and a mean absolute error of 0.82 months for predicted median progression-free survival, the time patients live without disease progression. For objective response rate—the share of patients with a measured tumor response—R² was 0.71 and mean absolute error was 7.3 percentage points. Combining organoid and clinical data significantly outperformed either data type alone.

articles.snippet:
Orakl Oncology, an artificial intelligence-driven biotechnology company developing technologies to improve the prediction of cancer drug responses, has raised $34 million in Series A funding co-led by Norrsken VC and Singular. The financing will support the company's continued expansion, international hospital partnerships, and development of its AI platform, which combines patient-derived tumor samples, clinical information, and experimental biological data to advance oncology drug research.

articles.text:
Orakl Oncology: $34 Million Series A Funding Co-Led By Norrsken VC And Singular To Expand AI-Powered Cancer Drug Discovery
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:56 AM
Orakl Oncology: $34 Million Series A Funding Co-Led By Norrsken VC And Singular To Expand AI-Powered Cancer Drug Discovery
Orakl Oncology, an artificial intelligence-driven biotechnology company developing technologies to improve the prediction of cancer drug responses, has raised $34 million in Series A funding co-led by Norrsken VC and Singular. The financing will support the company’s continued expansion, international hospital partnerships, and development of its AI platform, which combines patient-derived tumor samples, clinical information, and experimental biological data to advance oncology drug research.
The financing was announced by Diane-Laure Pagès, Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of Orakl Oncology, who highlighted the company’s growing network of cancer research partners and expansion plans. The company was founded in 2023 by Pagès, Fanny Jaulin, Ph.D., and Gustave Ronteix.
Orakl originated at Gustave Roussy, the French cancer research and treatment institution where Pagès completed her doctoral studies.
Since its founding, the company has expanded from three co-founders to a team of more than 40 scientists, engineers, AI researchers, and business professionals.
Approximately 30% of its employees hold doctoral degrees.
Orakl plans to establish additional teams in the United States and United Kingdom as it expands its international research and commercial operations.
Building AI Models Around Patient-Derived Cancer Biology
Orakl Oncology is developing an AI platform designed to improve the predictability of responses to cancer treatments.
A central component of its strategy involves generating and analyzing biological information derived from patient tumors.
Cancer treatment responses can vary significantly between patients, even when they have cancers classified within the same disease category.
These differences create challenges for pharmaceutical researchers seeking to identify which experimental medicines are most likely to demonstrate beneficial effects.
Orakl is addressing this problem by combining AI with experimentally generated biological data and associated clinical information.
The company believes training AI systems on information closely connected to actual patient biology can support more relevant drug development research.
Its technology is intended to help researchers understand relationships between tumor characteristics and responses to potential treatments.
Rather than relying exclusively on publicly available datasets, Orakl is building proprietary biological information through its research infrastructure and hospital collaborations.
This approach is designed to provide a foundation for developing AI models focused on oncology drug response prediction.
Expanding International Hospital Partnerships
Orakl has established a network of hospital partnerships supporting access to patient tumor samples and related clinical information.
The company signed five hospital partnerships during 2026.
It also expects more than 15 additional cancer centers across Europe, North America, and Asia to join its network.
These relationships are an important component of Orakl’s approach to developing its AI platform.
Participating hospitals provide research-ready tumor samples and clinical information that can be analyzed alongside laboratory-generated data.

articles.text:
Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 8:55 PM
Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded
Southland Holdings has secured a $34 million tunnel construction project in the Southwest along with additional contracts supporting data center construction in the Mid-Atlantic and Southwest. The awards expand activity across the company’s civil infrastructure business as demand continues for specialized construction services supporting transportation and digital infrastructure.
Two Southland subsidiaries within its Civil segment will perform the newly awarded work.
Southland Contracting received the $34 million tunnel project, which includes the design and installation of approximately 5,800 linear feet of liner-plate crossings.
The project scope also includes associated shafts, shoring, and grouting work.
The award adds to Southland’s tunnel construction operations, which form part of its broader infrastructure services business.
Separately, Oscar Renda Contracting secured a master service agreement to provide labor and equipment at a data center site in the Mid-Atlantic.
The subsidiary also received two contracts, including another master service agreement, for work at a data center location in the Southwest.
The data center agreements will provide construction-related labor and equipment services as directed by the customer.
Southland has not disclosed a final contract value for the data center work. The amount will depend on the actual quantities of services and equipment required during project execution.
The company also clarified that the data center agreements are project-specific and are not recurring contracts.
The awards provide Southland with additional exposure to the data center construction market, where infrastructure development requires specialized construction capabilities and supporting services.
Data centers depend on extensive physical infrastructure, including power systems, cooling equipment, utility connections, and supporting facilities. Construction activity in the sector creates opportunities for contractors involved in site preparation, civil engineering, and related infrastructure work.
Southland operates across several infrastructure markets, including bridges, tunneling, transportation, communications, marine construction, steel structures, water and wastewater treatment, and water pipelines.
Its subsidiaries provide specialized construction services for public and private sector projects throughout North America and internationally.
The company traces its roots to 1900 and is headquartered in Grapevine, Texas.
The latest awards reinforce the company’s participation in two infrastructure markets receiving substantial investment: underground transportation and utility infrastructure, and data center development.
The $34 million tunnel project provides a defined contract value, while the additional data center agreements create opportunities for further project revenue based on customer-directed work.
Southland did not provide project completion schedules or anticipated revenue recognition timelines for the new awards.

articles.text:
Zus Health: $33 Million Series B To Expand Connected Healthcare And AI Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 12:46 PM
Zus Health: $33 Million Series B To Expand Connected Healthcare And AI Platform
Zus Health has raised $33 million in Series B funding to expand its intelligent patient record platform, national healthcare data network, and artificial intelligence-powered clinical workflows. Drive Capital led the round, with participation from Sanofi Ventures, HealthX Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, F-Prime, Maverick Ventures, and JAZZ Venture Partners. The financing brings the company’s total capital raised to more than $100 million.
Founded in 2021, Zus is developing infrastructure that combines fragmented clinical information into a continuously updated patient record. Its technology is designed to give healthcare providers and applications access to more complete and actionable patient information without requiring each organization to build its own connectivity network.
The Zus Aggregated Profile creates a longitudinal patient record from information across electronic health record networks, pharmacies, laboratories, care-event notifications, and other clinical sources. An intelligence layer uses AI to organize that information and make it available through clinical and administrative workflows.
Zus supports pre-visit preparation, care transitions, risk adjustment, quality-gap closure, and population health management. Its Generated Patient Summaries transform fragmented records into concise information that clinicians and care teams can use during treatment.
The company’s national network supported more than 110 million transactions during August. Its AI-native clinical platform generated 39 million evidence citations during 2026 through the announcement date.
Zus also applied to become a Qualified Health Information Network under the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement. Its candidacy and HITRUST certification support its effort to participate in secure nationwide health information exchange.
The funding will be used to improve clinical intelligence, expand national data connectivity, increase record freshness, and support additional workflows across value-based and specialty care.
KEY QUOTES:
“The story of electronic medical records doesn’t end with the silos we have today. We’ve spent decades digitizing healthcare, but the information still doesn’t move with the patient. We’re building a networked medical record that changes that—connecting information across the healthcare system and making it available to the people and applications that need it. And now, with AI, we have an extraordinary opportunity to build workflows that actually make delivering care easier, faster, and more effective.”
Jonathan Bush, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Zus Health
“We believe healthcare is entering a new era in which AI can fundamentally change how care is delivered, but that transformation depends on having reliable, connected patient information. Zus has built the foundation to address that challenge at scale. Its combination of technology, market opportunity, and leadership gives us conviction in the company’s ability to help shape the next generation of healthcare.”
Molly Bonakdarpour, General Partner at Drive Capital

The latest funding brings Zus Health's total capital raised to more than $100 million. The company will use the investment to advance its intelligent patient record platform, expand its nationwide healthcare data network and develop AI-powered clinical workflows.
Zus Health, the health technology company founded by Jonathan Bush, has raised $33 million in Series B funding to expand its healthcare data infrastructure and develop AI-powered clinical workflows. The round was led by Drive Capital, with participation from Sanofi Ventures, HealthX Ventures, Alumni Ventures and existing investors Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), F-Prime, Maverick Ventures and JAZZ Venture Partners.
The latest funding brings Zus Health's total capital raised to more than $100 million. The company will use the investment to advance its intelligent patient record platform, expand its nationwide healthcare data network and develop AI-powered clinical workflows.
Founded in 2021, Zus Health has built an API-first, FHIR-native medical record platform designed to consolidate fragmented patient information into a continuously updated longitudinal health record. Its platform connects data from EHR networks, pharmacies, laboratories, care event notifications and other clinical sources, making patient information accessible through APIs, standalone applications, embedded components and direct EHR integrations.
The company's Zus Aggregated Profile (ZAP) combines fragmented clinical information into a unified patient record, supported by AI-powered clinical intelligence. The platform is designed to help healthcare organizations access a more complete view of patients without building their own data connectivity infrastructure.
According to Bush, the company has developed its platform in three layers: a nationwide patient record, a data network that continuously feeds information into the record, and AI-enabled workflows that automate care-related tasks.
"Electronic health record systems (EHRs) succeeded at digitizing healthcare but failed to make patient information portable across organizations," Bush, founder and CEO of Zus Health, told Fierce Healthcare.
The company currently works with value-based care organizations, digital health companies, provider organizations, and diagnostics and precision medicine companies. Its solutions support pre-visit preparation, transitions of care, risk adjustment, quality gap closure and population health management.
Zus reported that its nationwide network supported more than 110 million networked transactions in August, while its AI-native clinical platform generated 39 million evidence citations year-to-date across its solutions.
The company is also seeing growth in specialty care, particularly oncology, where patient records are often distributed across multiple providers. Its aggregated patient data is being used to support treatment eligibility reviews, clinical trial criteria assessments and genetic testing, reducing the manual effort involved in reviewing fragmented records.

articles.snippet: Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks SecurityWeek
articles.text:
Cloud Security
Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks
Created by Zerto and Kashya veterans, the startup has launched a platform designed to recover whole cloud applications.
By
SecurityWeek News
|
November 11, 2026 (6:16 AM ET)
Flipboard
Reddit
Whatsapp
Whatsapp
Email
Cloud application recovery startup Dreeze announced on Tuesday that it raised $33 million in a seed funding round as it emerged from stealth mode with a platform built to bring back whole cloud applications instead of only the data behind them.
The round was led by Norwest and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Claltech also investing.
Dreeze , whose staff is split between Israel and the United States, said the money will go toward product development, bigger sales and marketing teams, and getting its platform into more enterprises.
The company was formed in 2025 by Avi Raichel and brothers Ziv and Oded Kedem. The three previously worked together at Zerto, which HPE acquired , and Kashya.
Dreeze’s argument is that getting data back after an incident is not the same as getting an application running again. A cyberattack or a mistake by an AI agent can leave an organization with its data intact but without the configurations, secrets, infrastructure and connections the application needs.
Its platform, named Application Revival, scans the customer’s cloud environment on an ongoing basis, works out which resources and dependencies belong to which application, and generates a recovery plan from the live environment. Backups of data and configurations are stored with those recovery plans in an immutable, isolated vault under the customer’s control.
Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.
In a recovery scenario, Application Revival automatically reconstructs the application as a whole. Customers can also run recovery tests in an isolated account, with no impact on production.
“Companies have spent years getting better at backing up data, but getting the data back doesn’t mean the business is back,” said Ziv Kedem, the company’s CEO. “With cyber threats increasing and AI introducing new risks, enterprises need to assume that critical applications will go down.”
“We started Dreeze because recovery needs to go further. Our goal is to make Application Revival the new standard, so companies know they have a proven path to bring their applications back when something goes wrong,” he added.
The AWS version of the platform is generally available. Support for Microsoft Azure is in early access, with general availability expected in early 2027.

NEW YORK , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nidus, the robotics company deploying embodied intelligence inside America's defense factories, announced $30 million in funding today, backed by Kleiner Perkins and Costanoa, with participation from Ludlow Ventures, SF1, Absolute Partners, Tau, and angel investors, including Chris Power, founder of Hadrian; Adrian Aoun, co-founder of Dulo, Foundational Industries and Seneca; and Nikhil Goel, Chief Commercial Officer at Archer.
America's defense industrial base has a capacity crisis. The country that once produced more than half the world's goods now relies heavily on overseas supply chains to manufacture parts for its own weapons systems. This constitutes a national security risk, and factories urgently need to increase output to meet demand.
Nidus builds embodied intelligence that lets traditional industrial robots perform precision assembly tasks. The company develops and deploys foundation robotics models across America's critical defense factories, using sovereign AI training practices. This lets each customer retain its collective knowledge, which is crucial in secure environments.
"I grew up in rural South Carolina and watched offshoring create the current industrial base crisis," said Justin Sealy, co-founder and CEO of Nidus. "At this point, we can't out-labor or out-scale our competition. We need to leapfrog the rest of the world by deploying physical AI that scales America's existing industrial capacity. This is why we started Nidus."
Nidus is deploying across the defense industrial base and quickly eclipsed seven figures in revenue in its first four months. The company is currently delivering customized models to automate wire processing on its proprietary platform, which was built from the ground up to meet Department of War security requirements.
"In physical AI, the value will accrue to players that prioritize deployment and customer value. And Nidus is the rare team that has actually deployed AI into the most locked-down environments in the country" said Aatish Nayak, partner at Kleiner Perkins. "The demand they're seeing is a testament to the value of their mission and product. We're thrilled to back Justin, Charu, Harrison, and Cane as they bring AI to the factories America's security depends on."
"The U.S. cannot rebuild industrial capacity through new construction alone. Nidus is taking a different approach, using AI and robotics to increase production inside existing factories," said Greg Sands, Founder and Managing Partner at Costanoa. "We backed Justin and the team at pre-seed because of their firsthand experience with the challenges of American manufacturing and their technical ability to address them. We believe Nidus has the potential to make a meaningful difference in how critical products are manufactured in the U.S."
Nidus will use this funding to grow its engineering team, expand from wire-harness automation into additional factory workflows, and scale production deployments with U.S. defense manufacturers.

articles.snippet:
Tendrils has raised $30 million to develop a new processor architecture designed around thousands of parallel computing cores.

articles.text:
Tendrils Raises $30 Million To Rebuild General-Purpose Computing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:17 PM
Tendrils Raises $30 Million To Rebuild General-Purpose Computing
Tendrils has raised $30 million to develop a new processor architecture designed around thousands of parallel computing cores.
Benchmark led the round, with participation from Visionaries Club, the UK Sovereign AI Fund, FR8, Antimatter, Cloudberry VC, Conviction, Embassy Ventures, and SV Angel. Angel investors also participated, and Jack Altman has joined the company’s board.
Tendrils is attempting to redesign the central processing unit without the backward-compatibility constraints associated with conventional sequential and single-core architectures.
The company argues that modern CPUs continue to inherit architectural decisions dating back to the 1970s. In its view, cache-coherency protocols, reorder buffers, shared mutable memory, and linear instruction sequences create complexity that limits efficient scaling.
Rather than modifying existing architectures, Tendrils is building a processor intended to have thousands of cores operating in parallel. That approach requires the company to develop hardware and software together.
Tendrils is therefore working on Vine, an open-source programming language designed from the outset for parallel-first computer architectures. The company believes closer coordination between language design and processor architecture can eliminate legacy requirements and enable more scalable general-purpose computing.
The funding will support the research, engineering, and development required to turn this concept into functioning hardware and software. Tendrils is also recruiting hardware and software engineers interested in developing the architecture.
Although AI accelerators have demonstrated the value of highly parallel computing for specialized workloads, Tendrils is targeting general-purpose applications. The company’s objective is to create an architecture that can support a wider range of software without relying on the sequential design assumptions embedded in conventional processors.

articles.text:
Northwind Group: $30 Million Loan Supports 52-Unit Condominium Development Near Manhattan’s Union Square
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:25 AM
Northwind Group: $30 Million Loan Supports 52-Unit Condominium Development Near Manhattan’s Union Square
Northwind Group has originated a $30 million first-mortgage acquisition and predevelopment loan for a residential development site at 110 East 16th Street in Manhattan’s Union Square neighborhood. The financing will support Pro-H Group’s acquisition and redevelopment of the property into a planned 22-story condominium building with 52 residences.
The property is located on East 16th Street between Union Square East and Irving Place.
It is currently occupied by a vacant nine-story parking garage.
Pro-H Group plans to demolish the existing structure and develop a residential property containing a mixture of one- to four-bedroom condominium homes.
The proposed building will also include resident amenities.
The project is located near Union Square, an established neighborhood known for transportation connections, retail businesses, restaurants, and residential demand.
Northwind believes the site’s location makes it attractive for a high-end residential development.
The company cited limited availability of newly developed condominium units in Manhattan as an important consideration in its financing decision.
According to the announcement, Manhattan’s new development condominium inventory is at its lowest level in more than a decade.
Northwind expects the proposed property to address some of the demand for new housing in the Union Square area.
The $30 million financing was originated through Northwind Debt Fund III, also known as NDF III.
The fund recently completed its final close with approximately $1 billion in capitalization.
That amount was twice the fund’s initial $500 million target.
Northwind uses its debt funds to provide financing for residential properties and development opportunities in markets where new supply is limited.
Its strategy includes acquisition loans, predevelopment financing, and other credit investments involving real estate sponsors.
The financing for 110 East 16th Street provides capital for the acquisition and early development stage of the project.
Predevelopment financing can support activities such as design, planning, permitting, and other work required before construction begins.
Pro-H Group is a New York-based real estate development and construction organization founded by Burton Hung in 2006.
The company operates through an integrated model encompassing development, design, construction, and specialized facade systems.
It has completed more than 100 development and facade projects across New York City and New Jersey.
Its in-house capabilities include architects, engineers, construction professionals, and other specialists.
Pro-H intends to use this integrated experience to develop the Union Square condominium project.
The acquisition also extends its development activities in Manhattan.
Brown Harris Stevens Development Marketing is working with Pro-H Group on another residential project, Loggia NoMad.
That development is a 28-story, 94-unit condominium building at 842 Sixth Avenue that is currently in pre-sales.
Robin Schneiderman, Managing Director at Brown Harris Stevens Development Marketing, represented Pro-H Group in the Union Square property acquisition.
Jonathan Hageman, Managing Director of Capital Markets at JLL, represented the seller.
